
### buffer usage: fast to slow, store + forward 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/intro/texfig/store-forward-buffer-usage-fast-to-slow-store--forward.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1 fig-alt="*store and forward* switches are illustrated as taking in packets and buffering them as they received, and only sending packets after they are fully contained in the buffer. These are the most common type of switches, by far."}

![](/intro/texfig/store-forward-buffer-usage-fast-to-slow-store--forward.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="*store and forward* switches are illustrated as taking in packets and buffering them as they received, and only sending packets after they are fully contained in the buffer. These are the most common type of switches, by far."}


:::


### buffer usage: fast to slow, cut-through 

![](/intro/texfig/store-forward-buffer-usage-fast-to-slow-cut-through.figure.svg){fig-alt="*cut-through* switches are illustrated as sending packets as they are being received as long as no other packets are waiting. Though more efficient, these are uncommon as they are more difficult to implement than store-and-forward switches (because of, for example, error handling)"}
